The original paper trains BERT4Rec with random masked-item reconstruction and additionally generates examples masking only the final item; it does not specify a terminal-example sampling probability. Next-item inference appends [MASK] to the observed history and scores from that token’s final hidden representation. Terminal masking is therefore part of the original method, rather than a new objective. [Paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690#S3.SS6)

The official generator makes `dupe_factor` randomly masked copies plus one last-item-only copy of every training window. With `dupe_factor=10`, terminal-only examples constitute 1/11 of generated examples, not 1/11 of supervised targets; random masks can also include the last item. `masked_lm_prob` controls the number of selected positions; `mask_prob` controls replacement with [MASK]. The ML-1M script sets these to 0.2 and 1.0 respectively. `force_last=True` instead selects each user’s latest `max_seq_length` tokens and masks the final item for evaluation; ordinary training uses sliding windows and separately adds terminal examples. [Official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [ML-1M configuration](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh)

The implementation right-pads and uses learned absolute positions starting at zero. Evaluation truncates the sequence including its target to length N, then replaces that target with [MASK]: equivalently, retain at most N−1 history items and append [MASK]. For this harness’s required left padding, preserve the supplied positional convention and final-nonpadding readout. An allocation-only experiment should change terminal-example frequency while holding windows, retained context, positional IDs, corruption rules, and inference construction fixed; otherwise it also changes context or positional alignment. [Generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [Position embeddings](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/modeling.py)
